text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait bars employment of foreign workers under 21 years of age. Before the measure employers were allowed to hire 18-year-old workers.
- Kuwait's civil aviation authority fines Kuwait Airways Corp for permitting an aircraft to fly from London to Kuwait with three engines; fourth engine was out of order.

- Kuwait to naturalise maximum of 10,000 stateless people who claim to be Kuwaitis, sources say. About 100,000 stateless people, mostly Arabs, live in Kuwait and claim to be Kuwaitis. Kuwait says many have concealed original nationality documents.

- National Bank of Kuwait to join international institutions managing sale of shares in Santa Fe International, which earlier this month filed with U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for an initial public offering of up to 30 million ordinary shares.
- Kuwait and Lebanon exchange ratification documents for investment accord signed in Beirut in 1996.
- Austrian investors discuss investment prospects with Kuwait's Public Industry Authority.

- Kuwait's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah congratulates Jordan's King Hussein on the kingdom's national day. Relations between Jordan and Gulf Arab state were strained due to what Kuwait saw as Jordan's sympathy with Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait.
- Traffic department at Interior Ministry to launch one-month campaign in June against speeding and reckless driving.
